newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura says takes Japan SESC complaint seriously.
newsitem.headline: Nomura says takes Japan SESC complaint seriously.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Tuesday that it was taking a complaint filed by Japan's securities watchdog seriously and added that it would make a "fresh start".
Government sources said earlier on Tuesday that the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) had filed complaints with prosecutors against Nomura and three former Nomura executives.
"We are taking the complaints seriously," Nomura said in a statement.
"We will make a fresh start in order to prevent a recurrance of such events. We deeply apologise for the inconvenience the scandal has caused our customers and the public."

The complaints were filed following an SESC probe into allegations that the nation's biggest brokerage made illegal compensation payments of 49.7 million yen to a corporate client who has been linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer, the sources said.

Filing a complaint with prosecutors is the first step towards bringing legal action against a company or an individual. The SESC raided Nomura's offices in March in a widening probe into the brokerage's role in the payments.
Sokaiya typically try to extort money from firms by threatening to expose dubious business practices or to disturb shareholders' meetings.
Nomura made a sweeping reshuffle of its top management late last month, hoping to win back public trust. It has claimed that the company itself was not involved in the payoff scandal.
